Anthropic’s Revenue Could Soar From $47 Billion to $200 Billion by 2028 as Bankers Build a Massive AI Valuation Case Ahead of Its IPO: Report (UPDATED)

Anthropic is reportedly projecting up to $200 billion in 2028 revenue as bankers weigh a potential $2 trillion IPO valuation.

Editor’s note: The story has been updated to include a comment from Ivan Feinseth.

Anthropic reportedly expects $190 billion to $200 billion in revenue by 2028, far exceeding the $47 billion annualized revenue run rate reported in May.

## Bankers Reach Past Typical Timelines

Bankers are applying enterprise value-to-revenue multiples based on forecasts, Reuters reported on Friday, citing four sources.

Anthropic’s revenue run rate was about $9 billion at the end of 2025, then climbed to more than $47 billion by May.

For the second quarter of 2026, Anthropic expects revenue of at least $10.9 billion, more than double the previous quarter.

That would put the company on track to post its first quarterly operating profit, estimated at $559 million. Anthropic also said its revenue run rate increased more than tenfold annually in each of the three years through early 2026.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to Benzinga‘s request for comment.

Read Also: OpenAI and Anthropic May Be Cheaper Than Chinese AI After All

## Palantir, Cloudflare Set the Benchmark

According to the report, Palantir Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR), Cloudflare Inc. (NYSE:NET) and Space Exploration Technologies Corp (NASDAQ:SPCX) have become reference points for Anthropic’s valuation ahead of the company’s analyst day.

Palantir is trading at 53 times expected 2026 revenue, while Cloudflare trades at 41.6 times, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters.

Each company offers a different point of comparison.

Palantir reflects fast-growing businesses with exposure to AI. Cloudflare represents high-growth infrastructure companies. SpaceX represents a company valued more on its future growth potential than on its current earnings.

## Skeptics Question

Not everyone is convinced the math holds. “Could they get a $2 trillion valuation, yeah they could, and I just wonder if it would stay there over time,” David Merkel, a principal at Aleph Investments, told the publication.

He questioned whether AI truly “produces so much additional productivity” to justify the price.

Other investors, however, remain confident in the company’s prospects. Ivan Feinseth, chief investment officer at Tigress Financial Partners, told Benzinga that he is “very positive” about Anthropic’s underlying growth and long-term potential.

Feinseth pointed to the company’s rapid revenue growth, from $9 billion in late 2025 to $47 billion by mid-May, as evidence of genuine demand rather than speculative hype. He also cited Anthropic’s relationships with Alphabet Inc.’s (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google, Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) as strategic advantages.

At the same time, he identified several key risks, including uncertainty in forecasts, high capital requirements, dilution and growing competition from rivals.

Harvard Reveals $2.2 Billion SpaceX Stake, Its Largest Public Equity Holding: University's Bet on Elon Musk-led Company Outshines Amazon and Nvidia

Harvard disclosed a $2.2 billion stake in SpaceX, an early bet on Musk's rocket company that has grown since its June debut.

Harvard Management Co. disclosed a $2.2 billion stake in Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX), an early investment in Elon Musk‘s rocket company whose value became public for the first time following SpaceX’s blockbuster Nasdaq debut in June.

## A Bigger Bet Than Amazon or Nvidia

The university held 12.94 million shares of SpaceX Class A common stock as of June 30, according to a 13F filing disclosed on Friday.

The stake makes SpaceX Harvard’s largest disclosed public equity holding, well ahead of its next-largest positions in Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd. (NYSE:TSM), Cerebras Systems Inc (NASDAQ:CBRS) and Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA).

The SpaceX stake accounts for more than half of Harvard’s $4.3 billion in total U.S. equities disclosed in the filing.

At Friday’s closing price, Harvard’s stake would be worth approximately $1.81 billion.

The University of California’s investment arm also disclosed a stake in SpaceX, worth roughly $1 billion.

Read Also: TSMC’s Arizona Operations Poised for Bigger Profit This Year as Advanced Chip Demand Accelerates: Report

## SpaceX Stock’s Volatile Run

The company went public on the Nasdaq on June 12 and hit an all-time high of around $225 days later, before falling as low as around $104 in early August, a decline of more than 50% from its peak.

Shares have since rebounded after the company reported second-quarter revenue of $7.81 billion, up 92% year-over-year and ahead of the $6.93 billion analysts expected.

SpaceX’s rebound since its post-IPO plunge has also boosted Elon Musk’s net worth, which topped $858 billion last week, making him richer than Larry Page, Sergey Brin, and Jeff Bezos combined.

## Other Big Investors In SpaceX

Nvidia disclosed a $21 billion stake in SpaceX as of the end of the second quarter, according to its own 13F filing.

Google parent Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) disclosed a $94.1 billion stake in SpaceX, with about $80 billion of that stake that had been under short-term sale restrictions and the remaining $14.1 billion locked up through the third quarter of 2027.

Last week, Norway’s $2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund revealed a $1.22 billion stake in SpaceX, its first public disclosure of a position in the company.

Price Action: Shares of SpaceX closed 0.91% lower on Friday at $140 and gained 0.4% in extended trading.

text.analysis_text:
Stanley Druckenmiller Just Made a Big Bet on IREN While Dumping Broadcom, Intel and Micron

Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller added IREN to his $5.2B Q2 portfolio. See why he left chipmakers for AI data centers.

Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller is shifting his strategy. As his Duquesne Family Office portfolio expanded drastically in the second quarter of 2026, the legendary investor’s moves sent a clear message to Wall Street about overlooking the chipmakers’ hype and buying the infrastructure that powers them.

## A $5.2 Billion Portfolio

According to the firm’s latest 13F filings, Duquesne’s total portfolio value surged from roughly $3.37 billion in the first quarter of 2026 to $5.21 billion by the end of the second quarter.

During this massive capital deployment, Druckenmiller broadened his market exposure, expanding his overall holdings from 70 to 95 individual positions. A cornerstone of this expansion was a brand-new 87,100-share position in IREN Ltd. (NASDAQ:IREN), valued at nearly $3.98 million.

Read Also: Stanley Druckenmiller Bets Big on AMZN, AMD — Dumps AVGO, INTC and MU in Q2

## Druckenmiller Rotates Within the Chip Trade

Druckenmiller previously admitted he "screwed it up" by exiting his Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) holdings prematurely after seeing “disturbingly heated” signals in the broader tech sector. Now, he is aggressively cutting his exposure to traditional semiconductor manufacturing.

In the second quarter, Duquesne completely dumped its stakes in Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO), Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC), and Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU).

The firm also fully liquidated positions in chip-adjacent stocks like Lattice Semiconductor Corp. (NASDAQ:LSCC) and Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR), which were largely omitted in initial media reports.

While he did initiate a new 72,900-share stake in Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) and added 43,600 shares of Lam Research Corp. (NASDAQ:LRCX), the overriding trend was a distinct rotation out of legacy chipmakers.

## The Data Center Power Play

Instead of focusing solely on chipmakers, Druckenmiller also added exposure to digital-infrastructure and crypto-mining companies that are expanding into AI and high-performance computing.

IREN was not his only data center power play. Alongside this new position, Druckenmiller loaded up on other digital infrastructure operators. He purchased over 4 million shares of Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ:BTDR) and initiated a 754,800-share position in Riot Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:RIOT).

Furthermore, he quietly added 314,150 shares of Hut 8 Corp. (NASDAQ:HUT)—another critical infrastructure stock that slipped under the radar during early second-quarter reporting.

## How Has IREN Performed In 2026?

IREN shares rose 16.65% year-to-date, advanced 130.92% over the last year, and 4.36% over the last six months. It closed 1.56% lower at $44.06 per share on Friday, and it was 3.58% higher in pre-market trading on Monday.

Benzinga’s Edge Stock Rankings indicate that IREN maintains a weak price trend in the short, medium, and long terms, with a poor value score.

Harvard Did Not Sell Its Bitcoin ETF Holdings in Q2, Discloses No New Ethereum ETF Stake

Harvard University left its Bitcoin exchange-traded fund position unchanged in the second quarter, according to its latest 13F filing.

Harvard University left its Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) exchange-traded fund (ETF) position unchanged in the second quarter, according to its latest 13F filing released Friday.

## Harvard Holds Bitcoin ETF Position Steady

Harvard Management Co., a wholly owned subsidiary of Harvard University that manages its financial assets, reported holding 3.04 million shares of the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (NASDAQ:IBIT) as of June 30. The stake was worth $101.35 million based on IBIT’s price of 33.29 on June 30.

Harvard slashed its Bitcoin ETF stake significantly in the first quarter

What was previously Harvard’s top position, IBIT has slipped to eleventh place and currently represents 2.38% of the portfolio. Harvard bought the ETF first during the second quarter of 2025.

Meanwhile, Harvard bought no new stake in the spot Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) ETF after liquidating the position entirely in the first quarter.

The stake makes SpaceX Harvard’s largest holding, well ahead of its next-largest positions in Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd. (NYSE:TSM), Cerebras Systems Inc (NASDAQ:CBRS) and Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA).

Anthropic is reportedly projecting up to $200 billion in 2028 revenue as bankers weigh a potential $2 trillion IPO valuation.

Editor’s note: The story has been updated to include a comment from Ivan Feinseth.

Anthropic reportedly expects $190 billion to $200 billion in revenue by 2028, far exceeding the $47 billion annualized revenue run rate reported in May.

## Bankers Reach Past Typical Timelines

Bankers are applying enterprise value-to-revenue multiples based on forecasts, Reuters reported on Friday, citing four sources.

Anthropic’s revenue run rate was about $9 billion at the end of 2025, then climbed to more than $47 billion by May.

For the second quarter of 2026, Anthropic expects revenue of at least $10.9 billion, more than double the previous quarter.

That would put the company on track to post its first quarterly operating profit, estimated at $559 million. Anthropic also said its revenue run rate increased more than tenfold annually in each of the three years through early 2026.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to Benzinga‘s request for comment.

## Palantir, Cloudflare Set the Benchmark

According to the report, Palantir Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR), Cloudflare Inc. (NYSE:NET) and Space Exploration Technologies Corp (NASDAQ:SPCX) have become reference points for Anthropic’s valuation ahead of the company’s analyst day.

Harvard Reveals $2.2 Billion SpaceX Stake, Its Largest Public Equity Holding: University's Bet on Elon Musk-led Company Outshines Amazon and Nvidia

Harvard disclosed a $2.2 billion stake in SpaceX, an early bet on Musk's rocket company that has grown since its June debut.

Harvard Management Co. disclosed a $2.2 billion stake in Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX), an early investment in Elon Musk‘s rocket company whose value became public for the first time following SpaceX’s blockbuster Nasdaq debut in June.

## A Bigger Bet Than Amazon or Nvidia

The university held 12.94 million shares of SpaceX Class A common stock as of June 30, according to a 13F filing disclosed on Friday.

The stake makes SpaceX Harvard’s largest disclosed public equity holding, well ahead of its next-largest positions in Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd. (NYSE:TSM), Cerebras Systems Inc (NASDAQ:CBRS) and Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA).

The SpaceX stake accounts for more than half of Harvard’s $4.3 billion in total U.S. equities disclosed in the filing.

At Friday’s closing price, Harvard’s stake would be worth approximately $1.81 billion.

The University of California’s investment arm also disclosed a stake in SpaceX, worth roughly $1 billion.

## SpaceX Stock’s Volatile Run

The University of California’s investment arm also disclosed a stake in SpaceX, worth roughly $1 billion.

## SpaceX Stock’s Volatile Run

The company went public on the Nasdaq on June 12 and hit an all-time high of around $225 days later, before falling as low as around $104 in early August, a decline of more than 50% from its peak.

Shares have since rebounded after the company reported second-quarter revenue of $7.81 billion, up 92% year-over-year and ahead of the $6.93 billion analysts expected.

SpaceX’s rebound since its post-IPO plunge has also boosted Elon Musk’s net worth, which topped $858 billion last week, making him richer than Larry Page, Sergey Brin, and Jeff Bezos combined.

## Other Big Investors In SpaceX

Nvidia disclosed a $21 billion stake in SpaceX as of the end of the second quarter, according to its own 13F filing.

Google parent Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) disclosed a $94.1 billion stake in SpaceX, with about $80 billion of that stake that had been under short-term sale restrictions and the remaining $14.1 billion locked up through the third quarter of 2027.

Last week, Norway’s $2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund revealed a $1.22 billion stake in SpaceX, its first public disclosure of a position in the company.
